Duration::host¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

std::vector<std::int64_t> Duration::host() const

What It Extracts¶

host() copies every lane into an owning vector of signed 64-bit epoch-neutral nanosecond counts. It is the explicit boundary for code that needs standard C++ storage, serialization input, or interoperability with an API that does not understand Duration.

The result is flat and follows logical row-major order. Shape is deliberately not embedded in the vector; retain sizes() separately when the original N-D arrangement must be reconstructed. NaT is preserved as Duration::kNaT, and values remain exact beyond the integer precision of a floating-point representation.

Unlike sizes(), the returned vector owns its allocation. Mutating it cannot change the Duration. Extraction is therefore O(numel) in time and memory; prefer Duration operations when computation can remain inside Pluss.

Examples¶

Example 1. Preserve exact nanoseconds, including NaT.

const auto value = pluss::duration::nanos(
    {9'007'199'254'740'993LL, -1LL, pluss::Duration::kNaT});
const auto out = value.host();
std::cout << '[' << out[0] << ',' << out[1] << ',' << out[2] << "]\n";

Output¶

[9007199254740993,-1,-9223372036854775808]

Example 2. A matrix is flattened in logical row-major order and converted to nanoseconds regardless of its construction unit.

const auto value = pluss::make_duration(
    {1,2,3,4}, {2,2}, pluss::duration::Unit::Seconds);
const auto out = value.host();
std::cout << '[' << out[0] << ',' << out[1] << ','
          << out[2] << ',' << out[3] << "]\n";

Output¶

[1000000000,2000000000,3000000000,4000000000]

Example 3. The returned vector is independent storage.

const auto value = pluss::duration::minutes({15,30,45});
auto out = value.host();
out[0] = 0;
std::cout << "copy_first=" << out[0]
          << " source_first=" << value.host()[0] << "\n";

Output¶

copy_first=0 source_first=900000000000

Failure Modes¶

  • The returned vector has no shape metadata; flattening is intentional.

  • NaT remains the sentinel integer. Test with isnat() before handing data to software that may treat the minimum signed integer as an ordinary span.

  • Large arrays require a full host allocation and copy.

See Also¶

  • sizes: preserve N-D reconstruction metadata.

  • total().nanoseconds(): remain in Series rather than crossing to an STL container.

  • isnat: identify sentinel lanes before extraction.
